requirement:
`habeas author --all [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [-v|--verbose]` MUST author
the evidence of every current requirement and named example, together with the
reviews {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review` include, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`.
`--all` MUST be mutually exclusive with a subject name and `--stdout`. It MUST
also delete each orphaned citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and each orphaned site review
under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and report each deletion; the
deletion MUST NOT require model configuration or credentials.
Failure to discover declarations or to read, scan, or parse project sources MUST report an error,
not a successful empty batch.

Each subject MUST receive an independent assessment with its own prompt, inputs,
judgment, and usage record. The command MUST report aggregate completion and each
authoring error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.reporting`, and retain
successful writes when another assessment fails. It MUST return a nonzero
exit status if any assessment fails. False judgments MUST still be written as
completed assessments; they remain failures under ordinary evidence validation.
A denied mandatory input MUST abort only the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`. Interruption MUST instead stop the
whole batch: queued assessments MUST NOT start, running assessments MUST be
cancelled, and an assessment whose evidence has not been written when the
interruption arrives MUST NOT write it. Evidence already written MUST be
retained, and the command MUST report the number of assessments not started as
a batch failure.

The bundled Habeas skills MUST direct the supervising agent to run this command
to create or refresh evidence. They MUST leave judgments, rationales, and input
snapshots to the authoring harness; the supervising agent addresses findings by
changing requirements, source citations, implementation, or tests.

rationale:
I found no gap in `requirements.authoring.batch`. Every obligation has code reachable from the `{impl}` items and a test that asserts its outcome.

**Command shape and exclusivity**
- The `Command::Author` definition in `src/main.rs#fn[main]` and its clap attributes carry this. `--all` conflicts with `--stdout`. An `ArgGroup` makes `subject` and `all` mutually exclusive. `--missing` conflicts with `--force`.
- `main` dispatches `--all` to `author_all_with_options`, which calls `run_batch`.
- Tests: `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` checks exit code 2 and "cannot be used with" for subject plus `--all`, and for `--all` plus `--stdout`. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_stdout_is_rejected_before_authoring]` and `fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` cover the rest.

**Authoring every definition plus citation and site reviews, under refresh**
- `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[select_subjects]` selects every non-term definition, every citation-review item and every site. It counts current records as unchanged and selects everything under `--force`.
- Tests:
  - `fn[batch_fills_evidence_preserves_current_records_and_reauthors_only_changed_inputs]`
  - `fn[batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones]`
  - `fn[site_reviews_are_authored_by_requirement_and_orphans_deleted_by_all]`
  - the unit test `selection_includes_site_reviews_and_sites_of_selects_only_them`

**Orphan deletion**
- `fn[delete_orphaned_reviews]` removes citation and site reviews that no longer name an item or site. `run_batch` calls it before `config::resolve_authoring` and prints "Deleted orphaned review …" for each deletion.
- Tests: the unit test `fn[orphaned_citation_and_site_reviews_are_deleted]`, and the integration test `site_reviews_are_authored_by_requirement_and_orphans_deleted_by_all`, which removes the config and checks both the deletion and the stderr message.

**Discovery, read, scan and parse failures**
- `RepositoryInspection.discovery_errors` is populated in `src/evidence.rs#fn[inspect_repository_with_progress]` from declaration collection, source discovery and scanning, Rust read and parse errors, and queries that cannot run (`src/sites.rs#fn[discover]`). `run_batch` returns an error if it is non-empty, so an incomplete scan is never an empty batch or a source of false orphans.
- Tests: `fn[discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference]` covers a Rust parse error and an unclosed fence. `fn[unreadable_reference_sources_fail_the_batch_before_inference]` covers an unreadable source. `src/sites.rs#fn[a_query_that_cannot_run_is_a_discovery_error]` covers a failing site query.

**Independent assessments, failure handling and exit status**
- `run_batch` spawns one `prepare_assessment` task per subject, each with its own usage record. A failure is pushed to `outcome.failures` and reported, while other writes are retained. `main` prints the summary and returns an error, which gives a nonzero exit, when any failure exists. False judgments are written as completed assessments.
- Tests: `fn[failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure]` and `fn[terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors]` (the latter writes a false and a FIXME judgment). `fn[batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose]` covers the reporting split between default and verbose.

**Denied mandatory input**
- Only an `Interrupted` error cancels the batch (`fn[cancel_on_error]`), so a denial aborts one assessment while the queued ones continue.
- Test: `fn[a_denied_mandatory_input_aborts_only_its_assessment]` runs with concurrency 1, so the later assessments were queued. It checks a nonzero exit, a diagnostic naming the path, no request, no evidence, a `failed` usage record, and the others' evidence retained.

**Interruption**
- `run_batch` listens for ctrl-c and sets the watch via `stop`. It stops launching tasks, cancels running ones, discards any judgment not yet written (the check on `cancellation.borrow()` before `write_record`), and records "N assessments not started" as a `batch` failure.
- Test: `fn[interrupted_terminal_progress_keeps_unstarted_work_incomplete]` (via `assert_interruption_stops_the_batch`, with concurrency 1 and 2) checks:
  - a nonzero exit;
  - the "not started" message;
  - fewer than 6 requests;
  - exactly one record written;
  - a `cancelled` usage record with `evidence_written` false.

**Skills**
- `habeas-evidence`, `habeas-requirements` and `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` direct the agent to run `habeas author --all` and forbid writing judgments, rationales or inputs. Test: `fn[bundled_skills_direct_the_agent_to_the_authoring_harness]`.

The remaining output (policy and skipped counts, cache warmup, coverage-loss reviews) is specified by other requirements the same code marks `{impl}`.

:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. The reviewer MUST assess, for each citation,
whether the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition
changes, and whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
:::{req} site_review
Every site of a distributed requirement under
{cite}`requirements.references.distributed` MUST have a site review: an
assessment of whether that site upholds the requirement, recorded at
`evidence/sites/<full-name>/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` and
`<selector>` are encoded as under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. The review MUST use the prompt
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.site_prompt`. Mandatory inputs, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the site's outline
node, the requirement's complete declaration, and each declaration the
requirement cites. The record MUST contain the requirement's full name, the
site's file and selector, `queries`, the sorted names of the queries with a
match at the site, `applies`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`, with
determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. `applies` MUST be a
Boolean recording whether the requirement applies to the site. A site to which
the requirement does not apply MUST be judged `true`, and the rationale MUST
explain why it does not apply. `habeas info` MUST report, for each selected
distributed requirement, how many of its sites the requirement does not apply
to.
Validation MUST require a current, accepted review for every site, MUST report a
false review with its rationale, and MUST report stale, missing, or orphaned
reviews; a review is orphaned when its file and selector no longer name a site
of the requirement. A `{fixme}` naming the requirement inside a site
acknowledges a gap at that site only: it MUST be an input to that site's review
and MUST NOT contribute to the requirement's own review, coverage, or reference
set. A review MUST become stale when the site's hash, the requirement's
declaration, a cited declaration, its `queries`, or the `{fixme}` references
naming the requirement inside the site, with the words of their bodies, change.
Each site review's determination MUST be checked on its own, independently of
the requirement's evidence. Authoring with `--all` MUST include site reviews,
`habeas author sites:<full-name>` MUST author the site reviews of the named
requirement, and `habeas author sites:<full-name>/<file>#<selector>` MUST author
the review of the one site it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>` names the
file's root node. `habeas status` MUST report missing, stale, invalid, and false
site reviews with their requirement, file, and selector, and `habeas info` MUST
list each selected requirement's sites with their determinations.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
:::{req} reporting
By default, authoring MUST suppress per-subject `true` judgment lines and show
each `false` judgment's subject and outcome on stderr, on both terminals and
redirected output. Existing progress counters and completion summaries MUST remain
available; FIXME notices and authoring errors MUST remain visible. Single-subject
authoring MUST retain its subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and
usage-record metadata.
`-v` and `--verbose` MUST additionally show each false judgment's recorded Markdown
rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded
input snapshots. Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result,
without additional inference. In `--stdout` mode, stdout MUST remain only the
evidence JSON; verbose rationale and other diagnostics MUST go to stderr.
Verbosity MUST NOT change persistence, validation, or exit-status rules.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.invocation` {cite}`requirements.authoring.batch`
:::{req} read_denial.mandatory
When source-access policy denies a mandatory input, the assessment MUST abort
before any model request and report the denied path and reason to its caller;
for an untracked file, the report MUST say what {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.untracked`
says. The aborted assessment MUST NOT write evidence or emit evidence JSON, and
its usage record MUST identify the failure. In a batch, other assessments MUST
continue, including queued assessments, and their successful writes MUST be
retained; the command MUST return a nonzero exit status after the batch
finishes.
:::{req} concurrency
Each named authoring configuration MUST accept an optional positive integer
`concurrency` in its configuration table. When omitted, the maximum number of
simultaneous assessments MUST default to the number of available logical CPUs
for Bedrock, falling back to one when that count is unavailable, and to one for
Ollama. A configured value MUST override the default for either backend; zero
MUST be rejected as invalid configuration.
Batch authoring MUST use asynchronous tasks on a runtime with a fixed worker
thread pool. The number of assessments running at once MUST NOT exceed the
selected concurrency. Each assessment MUST retain its own model conversation and
usage record. Transient provider failures, including throttling, MUST be
retried within the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`; every other provider error MUST
be reported through the ordinary assessment-failure path.
:::{req} usage_storage
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
:::{req} persistence
After one valid judgment, the harness MUST write the subject text, submitted
determination and rationale, and recorded inputs using the existing evidence
schema. {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`
By default, it MUST write the subject's evidence file. With `--stdout`, it MUST
emit a single evidence JSON object followed by a newline to stdout and MUST NOT
create or change evidence files or directories. All three outcomes MUST be
written to the selected destination as completed assessments; their validation
status MUST follow {cite}`requirements.ci.determination`.
